intro: The fifth screen read the set better than any before it (all items 0.97, up from 0.94; every contradiction caught; one misread in 266 items), and 60 of 64 templates pass the legibility gate, up from 55. The giant fork, after failing three screens, scored full marks in both set pictures: "sweeping a small pile of litter and dust using a giant silver fork instead of a broom, which looks absurd". Eight of the nine templates v0.8 redrew pass; the lost balloon is still hedged ("let go, or just floating past"). Three templates that passed before slip on their new pictures (the heavy seesaw, the dog begging and the person about to trip), each for a reason the pictures show.
screen: Contradictions rose from 0.82 to 1.00: all 11 in the set and all 9 in the probes were noticed and explained, the fork's included. Actions rose to 0.97 and unintended oddities fell to 1.5 per picture. Inferences held at 0.83: of the 5 inference points the set lost, 4.5 belong to the four templates that fail the gate (below) and half a point to a kite that "may be stuck in the tree". The one misread was a walking woman's small red book, taken for a phone.
redrawn: The fork, the stalking cat, the dog at the door, the stealing bird, the sandbox, the grazing goat, the wave and the rain coming all pass, seven of them with full marks. The stalking cat was once "running toward" the bird in the busiest playground; the other three readers saw it "crouched low ... creeping". One reader of the fork added that it "could also be read as a pitchfork or garden fork, but either way it is the wrong tool". The lost balloon now floats just above the child, but every reader hedged the letting go: "could belong to the boy, who has just let go of it, or it could simply be floating past".
gate: Every template was screened in at least two pictures. The heavy seesaw fails because v0.8 made ordinary seesaws tip toward the heavier rider: a tipped seesaw is no longer the cue, and a reader saw the stranded girl as ordinary play ("the bigger boy is down and the smaller girl is up, so this doesn't look wrong"). The dog begging lost its inference where a grandmother's apple read as "a cherry ... or a red clown nose". The person about to trip was misread once (the small red book as a phone) and once missed where the box lay beside the walker rather than in the path.
